source: Hand-authored by Evidentia. Maps the eight FDA Section 524B premarket security control categories to the most relevant ISO 14971:2019 risk-management clause(s). ISO 14971 clause titles paraphrased in Evidentia's own words; no normative ISO text reproduced.
verification_note: These mappings are ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual links authored by Evidentia, not independently audited and not endorsed by the FDA or ISO. They are intended to orient a reader between the 524B security control categories and the ISO 14971 safety-risk-management process; they are not a control-equivalence assertion. Consumers MUST verify any reliance against the licensed ISO 14971:2019 text and the FDA guidance.
risk_model_note: Safety risk management (ISO 14971:2019) characterizes risk as a combination of the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm (commonly operationalized as probability × severity). Security risk management (ANSI/AAMI SW96:2023, building on AAMI TIR57:2016 (R2023)) characterizes security risk in terms of exploitability rather than probability of occurrence, while sharing the same patient-harm severity axis — a security exploit is assessed by how readily it can be carried out (exploitability) combined with the severity of the resulting patient harm. The FDA Section 524B premarket security controls feed the device's security risk management, which in turn informs the ISO 14971 safety risk file via the shared severity axis. This characterization is a paraphrase of the ISO 14971 and AAMI SW96/TIR57 methodologies, not a quotation from the FDA guidance or the standards.

mappings.notes: Illustrative conceptual link: authentication is a security risk-control measure that reduces the risk of unauthorized access; it is implemented under the risk-control activity. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.
Illustrative conceptual link: authorization is a security risk-control measure constraining what an authenticated entity may do. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.

Illustrative conceptual link: cryptographic protection of data confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity is a risk-control measure. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.

Illustrative conceptual link: identifying integrity-related hazards (unauthorized modification of code/data/execution) is part of risk analysis. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.
Illustrative conceptual link: integrity-verification mechanisms are risk-control measures. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.
Illustrative conceptual link: protecting sensitive data from disclosure is a risk-control measure. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.

mappings.target_control_title: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 10 — Production and post-production activities
mappings.notes: Illustrative conceptual link: security-event detection and logging supply the monitoring data feeding the production / post-production information-collection activity. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.

Illustrative conceptual link: resiliency and recovery capabilities are risk-control measures that preserve essential safe operation during and after a cybersecurity event. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.

mappings.target_control_title: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 8 — Evaluation of overall residual risk
mappings.notes: Illustrative conceptual link: the residual ability to recover safe operation informs the evaluation of overall residual risk. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.

mappings.target_control_title: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 10 — Production and post-production activities
mappings.notes: Illustrative conceptual link: the ability to securely update and patch over the lifecycle is the remediation arm of post-production risk management. Not independently audited — verify against the licensed standard.
